# Technical Specification

# 1. Introduction

## 1.1 Executive Summary

This Technical Specification documents an intentionally minimal Node.js repository. The entire codebase consists of **four files and 39 lines of content** at the repository root, with no subdirectories: `README.md`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, and `server.js`. Readers should calibrate expectations accordingly — this specification describes a deliberately small, self-contained artifact rather than a multi-module enterprise application, and every statement below is grounded in the four files that exist.

### 1.1.1 Project Overview

The repository presents itself under two different names, and both are documented facts rather than errors to be resolved by this specification:

| Identifier | Value | Declared In |
|---|---|---|
| Repository / document title | `hao-backprop-test` | `README.md` (line 1) |
| npm package name | `hello_world` | `package.json`, `package-lock.json` |
| Package version | `1.0.0` | `package.json`, `package-lock.json` |
| Package description | "Hello world in Node.js" | `package.json` |

Functionally, the project is a single-file HTTP server. `server.js` requires only Node.js's built-in `http` module, binds a listener to the loopback address `127.0.0.1` on port `3000`, and answers **every** inbound request with an identical fixed response: HTTP status `200`, header `Content-Type: text/plain`, and the 14-byte body `Hello, World!` followed by a newline. The request object is never inspected, so path, HTTP method, query string, headers, and request body have no effect on the outcome. On successful bind, the process writes a single line to standard output announcing its URL.

The dependency footprint is zero. `package.json` declares neither `dependencies` nor `devDependencies`, and `package-lock.json` (`lockfileVersion: 3`) contains only the root package record with no locked third-party packages. The project therefore runs on an unmodified Node.js installation with no installation step required.

### 1.1.2 Core Business Problem

The only purpose statement anywhere in the repository is the single sentence in `README.md`: it identifies the repository as a test project for "backprop integration" and instructs readers not to modify it. No product brief, business case, requirements document, issue tracker, or design note exists in the repository to elaborate further.

Interpreted strictly from that statement plus the observable implementation, the problem being solved is the need for a **known-good, zero-variance target repository** against which an external integration (referred to in the README as "backprop") can be exercised end to end. Integration and pipeline tooling requires a subject that is small enough to reason about completely, free of dependency resolution and build steps that could fail for unrelated reasons, and deterministic enough that any deviation in observed behavior indicates a fault in the tooling rather than in the subject. Every design choice visible in `server.js` — core-module-only imports, hardcoded constants, a response that ignores its input — serves that determinism requirement.

The README's explicit "Do not touch!" directive is a first-class functional requirement of this system, not incidental commentary: the artifact's value depends on its content remaining stable, because a fixture that changes cannot serve as a fixed reference point.

### 1.1.3 Key Stakeholders and Users

The repository contains no stakeholder register, ownership file, `CODEOWNERS`, or contribution guide. The following parties are the only ones evidenced, together with the audiences implied by the artifact's design and its README directive.

| Stakeholder / User | Evidence In Repository | Relationship to the System |
|---|---|---|
| Package author `hxu` | `author` field in `package.json` | Declared author of the npm package metadata |
| Committer `Sandeep01Kumar` | Sole commit `1a0874d` ("Add files via upload") | Uploaded all four files into the repository |
| Integration / automation engineers | README directive "Do not touch!" | Consume the repository as a fixture; the directive is addressed to anyone who might alter it |
| Automated tooling ("backprop") | README purpose statement | Named consuming context for which the project acts as an integration subject |

No end-user population is served by the running service. The HTTP endpoint performs no authentication, authorization, session handling, or user identification of any kind, so all callers are anonymous and indistinguishable, and every caller receives byte-identical output.

### 1.1.4 Value Proposition and Expected Impact

The repository states no business objectives, revenue expectations, adoption targets, or return-on-investment claims, and this specification does not manufacture any. What follows is the value proposition **as implemented** — each item is a directly verifiable property of the code and manifests rather than a projection.

| Value Delivered | Implementation Evidence | Practical Benefit |
|---|---|---|
| Complete determinism | Fixed `200` / `text/plain` / 14-byte body for every request; request object never read | Any observed deviation isolates the fault to the consuming tooling |
| Zero dependency risk | No `dependencies`/`devDependencies`; lockfile holds only the root package | No registry access, install failures, transitive CVEs, or version drift |
| Near-zero cognitive load | 14 lines in `server.js`; 39 lines repository-wide; no subdirectories | The entire system can be read and fully understood in seconds |
| No build or transpile step | CommonJS `require`; no bundler, compiler, or build configuration present | The source that is committed is exactly the source that executes |
| Contained blast radius | Listener bound to `127.0.0.1`, verified unreachable on non-loopback interfaces | Exercising the fixture cannot expose a network-facing surface |
| Stable reference baseline | Single commit, clean working tree, README "Do not touch!" | The fixture remains a fixed point of comparison over time |

The corresponding trade-off is equally deliberate and must be stated plainly: the repository offers no configurability, no routing, no error handling, no test coverage, no observability instrumentation, and no deployment automation. These absences are catalogued and bounded in section 1.3, and they are consistent with an artifact whose function is to be a fixture rather than a production service.


## 1.2 System Overview

### 1.2.1 Project Context

#### 1.2.1.1 Business Context and Positioning

The repository contains no market analysis, product positioning, competitive assessment, pricing model, roadmap, or commercial documentation of any kind. There is no `docs/` directory, no design notes, and no issue or pull-request templates. The `README.md` file is the sole narrative document, and it is two lines long.

Consequently, the only defensible positioning statement is the one the repository makes about itself: it is an **internal test fixture for an integration named "backprop"**, not a market-facing product. Two secondary signals corroborate this framing. First, the npm metadata is that of a canonical tutorial artifact — package name `hello_world`, description "Hello world in Node.js" — indicating the code was never intended as a differentiated product. Second, the hosting repository is named `28-july-existing-projects-qa-test-01`, a dated quality-assurance test identifier rather than a product name. The MIT license declared in both `package.json` and `package-lock.json` is the only distribution-related term expressed, and no `LICENSE` file accompanies it.

#### 1.2.1.2 Current System Limitations

No predecessor system, legacy platform, or migration path is referenced anywhere in the repository, so this project is not documented as replacing or upgrading anything. The limitations below are therefore properties of the current implementation itself, each confirmed by direct inspection and, where noted, by executing the server.

| Limitation | Evidence | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Loopback-only reachability | `hostname = '127.0.0.1'` (`server.js` line 3); requests to the host's routable address fail while `127.0.0.1:3000` succeeds | Cannot serve any client outside the host machine |
| Hardcoded network configuration | `hostname` and `port` are literal constants; no `process.env` reference exists anywhere in the codebase | Host and port cannot be changed without editing source |
| No request differentiation | The handler never reads `req`; no `req.url` or `req.method` reference exists | Routing, methods, query strings, and payloads are all inert |
| No error handling | No `try`/`catch` and no `'error'` event listener anywhere | A bind failure (for example, port 3000 already in use) surfaces as an unhandled exception |
| No graceful shutdown | No `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT` handler and no `process.exit` call | The process can only be terminated abruptly |
| Unresolvable declared entry point | `package.json` sets `main` to `index.js`, but no `index.js` file exists | Consumers must invoke `server.js` explicitly; module resolution via the package name would fail |
| No `start` script | `scripts` contains only `test` | There is no conventional `npm start` path to launch the server |
| No automated verification | `npm test` runs `echo "Error: no test specified" && exit 1` and exits with code 1 | Any CI gate wired to `npm test` fails by design |
| Naming inconsistency | README title `hao-backprop-test` versus package name `hello_world` | The artifact is discoverable under two unrelated identifiers |
| No runtime version constraint | No `engines` field, `.nvmrc`, or `.node-version` file | The supported Node.js range is undeclared |

#### 1.2.1.3 Integration with the Existing Landscape

At the code level there is no integration surface beyond the inbound HTTP listener. Static inspection of every file confirms the complete absence of database clients, message brokers, caches, outbound HTTP or API calls, authentication providers, credential material, environment-variable configuration, and third-party SDKs — the only `require` statement in the repository imports Node.js's built-in `http` module.

| Integration Dimension | Observed State |
|---|---|
| Inbound interface | One HTTP listener on `127.0.0.1:3000`, accepting any method and path |
| Outbound interfaces | None; no network clients or external service calls exist |
| Persistence | None; no database, file, or in-memory store is written or read |
| Configuration source | Source-code literals only; no environment variables or config files |
| Telemetry / logging | A single `console.log` line to standard output at startup |
| Package registry | None required at runtime; the lockfile resolves zero third-party packages |
| Source control | Hosted on GitHub as `28-july-existing-projects-qa-test-01`, branch `main` |

The meaningful integration is therefore **ecosystem-level rather than code-level**: the repository is consumed as an input by the external "backprop" tooling named in the README, using standard Git and npm conventions — clone the repository, read the manifests, optionally install (a no-op), and execute the entry script. The system integrates by being a well-formed, conventional Node.js package, not by calling anything.

### 1.2.2 High-Level Description

#### 1.2.2.1 Primary System Capabilities

The system implements exactly three observable capabilities. All three were verified by running `node server.js` and issuing requests against it.

| Capability | Behavior | Verification |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP listener | Accepts TCP connections on `127.0.0.1:3000` | Connection succeeds on loopback; fails on the host's routable IP |
| Fixed response generation | Returns `200`, `Content-Type: text/plain`, and a 14-byte `Hello, World!` body to every request | `GET /`, `POST /anything/else?q=1` with a body, and `DELETE /deep/path` all produced identical results |
| Startup announcement | Writes `Server running at http://127.0.0.1:3000/` to standard output once bound | Observed on process start |

No other capability exists. There is no static file serving, no content negotiation, no compression, no CORS handling, no health endpoint distinct from the default response, no rate limiting, and no TLS.

#### 1.2.2.2 Major System Components

The system is a single operating-system process with no internal module boundaries. "Components" here means the distinct responsibilities visible within `server.js` plus the supporting repository artifacts.

| Component | Artifact | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP transport | Node.js built-in `http` module (`server.js` line 1) | Connection handling, request parsing, response serialization |
| Server instance | `http.createServer(...)` (`server.js` lines 6–10) | Owns the request-handling callback |
| Request handler | Inline arrow function (`server.js` lines 7–9) | Sets status `200`, sets `Content-Type`, ends the response with the fixed body |
| Listener and startup logger | `server.listen(...)` (`server.js` lines 12–14) | Binds host and port; logs the startup URL |
| Configuration constants | `hostname`, `port` (`server.js` lines 3–4) | Supply the bind address and port as literals |
| Package manifest | `package.json` | Declares identity, version, `main`, license, and the `test` script |
| Dependency lockfile | `package-lock.json` | Pins the root package; records zero third-party dependencies |
| Project documentation | `README.md` | States the fixture purpose and the do-not-modify directive |

The following diagram shows the runtime request flow and the loopback boundary that contains it.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Client["HTTP Client<br/>curl, browser, or automated harness"]

    subgraph Host["Single Host - Loopback Interface 127.0.0.1"]
        Listener["TCP Listener<br/>port 3000"]
        Handler["Inline Request Handler<br/>request object never inspected"]
        Fixed["Fixed Response<br/>status 200, text/plain, 14-byte body"]
        Log["Startup Log<br/>single line to standard output"]
        Listener --> Handler
        Handler --> Fixed
        Listener --> Log
    end

    Client -->|"any method, any path, any body"| Listener
    Fixed -->|"identical response every time"| Client
    External["Client on Any Non-Loopback Interface"] -.->|"connection not established"| Listener
```

#### 1.2.2.3 Core Technical Approach

Six architectural choices characterize the implementation, and each is directly observable in the source.

| Approach | Evidence | Rationale as Implemented |
|---|---|---|
| Core modules only | Sole `require` targets Node's built-in `http` | Eliminates installation, registry, and version-drift failure modes |
| CommonJS module system | `require(...)` with no `"type"` field in `package.json` | Runs on a default Node.js configuration with no build step |
| Single-file executable script | All logic in `server.js`; no exports declared | The listener opens as a side effect of evaluating the file |
| Stateless request handling | No variables mutated per request; no session or persistence | Each request is fully independent; no cross-request coupling |
| Configuration by literal constant | `hostname` and `port` declared as `const` | Behavior is fixed at author time, guaranteeing reproducibility |
| Input-independent response | `req` is accepted by the handler but never read | Output cannot vary with client behavior |

The response construction itself is three statements:

```javascript
res.statusCode = 200;
res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/plain');
res.end('Hello, World!\n');
```

Because the code sets no other headers, the remaining response headers observed on the wire — `Content-Length`, `Date`, `Connection: keep-alive`, and `Keep-Alive: timeout=5` — are supplied by Node.js `http` runtime defaults and are **not** configured by this repository. Any change to those defaults in a future Node.js release would change the observed response headers without any change to this codebase.

### 1.2.3 Success Criteria

#### 1.2.3.1 Measurable Objectives

The repository declares no acceptance criteria, service-level objectives, or performance targets. The objectives below are derived exclusively from behavior that the code guarantees and that can be asserted deterministically; each was confirmed during inspection.

| Objective | Verifiable Assertion | Confirmed Result |
|---|---|---|
| Process starts and binds | `node server.js` binds `127.0.0.1:3000` without error | Bound successfully |
| Startup log is exact | Standard output equals `Server running at http://127.0.0.1:3000/` | Matched exactly |
| Status code is invariant | Every response carries HTTP `200` | `200` for `GET`, `POST`, and `DELETE` |
| Content type is invariant | Every response carries `Content-Type: text/plain` | Present on all responses |
| Payload is byte-exact | Response body is `Hello, World!` plus a newline, 14 bytes | 14 bytes returned on every request |
| Input independence holds | Path, query, method, and body do not alter the response | Identical responses across all probes |
| Dependency count is zero | `package-lock.json` contains only the root package entry | Zero third-party packages |
| Isolation is enforced | Non-loopback interfaces cannot reach port 3000 | Connection attempt failed |
| Test script fails by design | `npm test` terminates with exit code 1 | Exit code 1 |

#### 1.2.3.2 Critical Success Factors

Four factors determine whether the artifact continues to serve its stated purpose. All four derive from the README's fixture framing and the implementation's design.

- **Content immutability.** The README's "Do not touch!" instruction is the project's governing constraint. The fixture's usefulness as a fixed reference collapses if its files change, and the single-commit history with a clean working tree reflects that stability today.
- **Dependency-free execution.** Zero declared and zero locked dependencies mean the project cannot fail for reasons of registry availability or transitive version conflict.
- **Port 3000 availability on the loopback interface.** With no error handling and no configuration override, the process depends on that specific address and port being free.
- **A CommonJS-capable Node.js runtime.** Since no `engines` constraint is declared, the operating assumption is any Node.js version providing `require` and the standard `http` API.

#### 1.2.3.3 Key Performance Indicators

The repository defines **no** key performance indicators. This is a verified absence, not an omission from this document: there is no metrics library, no instrumentation, no tracing, no health-check endpoint distinguishable from the default response, no logging framework, no latency or throughput target, no error budget, and no monitoring, alerting, or dashboard configuration in any file. No SLA or SLO is stated anywhere.

The only quantifiable, code-derived indicators available for the artifact are correctness and footprint constants rather than performance metrics:

| Indicator | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP status code returned | `200`, unconditionally | `server.js` line 7 |
| Response payload size | 14 bytes | `res.end('Hello, World!\n')`, measured on the wire |
| Distinct routes served | 1 (all paths share one handler) | `server.js` lines 6–10 |
| Bind address and port | `127.0.0.1:3000` | `server.js` lines 3–4 |
| Third-party dependencies | 0 | `package.json`, `package-lock.json` |
| Automated tests | 0 (test script exits 1) | `package.json` `scripts.test` |
| Total source lines | 39 across 4 files | Repository file inventory |
| Commits in history | 1 | Git history |

Any performance, availability, or reliability target for this system would have to be established by the consuming tooling; none can be sourced from this repository.


## 1.3 Scope

Scope for this system is unusually easy to delimit: the repository is four files totalling 39 lines, so the boundary between what exists and what does not is unambiguous. Everything listed as in-scope below was read in the source; everything listed as out-of-scope was confirmed absent by explicit inspection of the repository, not assumed.

### 1.3.1 In-Scope

#### 1.3.1.1 Core Features and Functionalities

**Must-have capabilities.** These are the capabilities the system actually delivers, and they constitute the whole of its functional surface.

| Capability | Definition of Correct Behavior | Implementing Artifact |
|---|---|---|
| Bind an HTTP listener | Listen on `127.0.0.1` port `3000` | `server.js` lines 3–4, 12 |
| Answer all requests uniformly | Status `200`, `Content-Type: text/plain`, body `Hello, World!` plus newline | `server.js` lines 6–10 |
| Announce startup | Emit `Server running at http://127.0.0.1:3000/` to standard output | `server.js` lines 12–14 |
| Declare package identity | Name `hello_world`, version `1.0.0`, MIT license, `test` script | `package.json` |
| Guarantee a zero-dependency install | Lockfile resolving only the root package | `package-lock.json` |
| State purpose and immutability | Fixture purpose and the do-not-modify directive | `README.md` |

**Primary user workflows.** No workflow documentation exists in the repository, so the workflows below are those the artifacts make possible; each was exercised or verified during inspection.

| Workflow | Steps | Observed Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Launch the service | Execute `server.js` with the Node.js runtime | Listener binds; startup line printed |
| Exercise the endpoint | Send any HTTP request to `http://127.0.0.1:3000/` | `200` with the 14-byte fixed body |
| Resolve dependencies | Run an npm install against the manifests | No third-party packages to fetch |
| Invoke the test script | Run `npm test` | Prints "Error: no test specified"; exits 1 |
| Inspect as a fixture | Clone the repository and read all four files | Full comprehension of the system |

The launch workflow warrants emphasis: because `package.json` declares no `start` script and its `main` field points to a non-existent `index.js`, the server must be started by naming `server.js` directly. There is no conventional npm-mediated launch path.

**Essential integrations.** Only two integration points are in scope, both internal to the host.

| Integration | Nature | Direction |
|---|---|---|
| Node.js built-in `http` module | Runtime API for transport and message handling | In-process |
| Process standard output | Destination for the single startup log line | Outbound, local |

**Key technical requirements.** These are the operating preconditions the code implies.

| Requirement | Basis |
|---|---|
| A Node.js runtime supporting CommonJS `require` and the `http` API | `server.js` line 1; no `"type"` field in `package.json` |
| TCP port `3000` free on the loopback interface | Hardcoded `port`; no error handling for bind failure |
| npm capable of reading `lockfileVersion: 3` for manifest operations | `package-lock.json` lockfile format |
| No installation, build, transpile, or bundling step | Zero dependencies; no build configuration present |
| Repository content remains unmodified | `README.md` directive "Do not touch!" |

#### 1.3.1.2 Implementation Boundaries

**System boundary.** The system is one Node.js process on one host. Its boundary is the TCP socket bound to `127.0.0.1:3000` plus the process's standard output stream. Nothing crosses that boundary in the outbound direction except HTTP responses and the startup log line. Verified by execution: `127.0.0.1:3000` served requests while the host's routable address refused the connection, so the loopback interface is a hard boundary and not merely a default.

**User groups covered.** Exactly one, undifferentiated: any anonymous HTTP client that can reach the loopback interface of the host. There are no roles, permissions, tenants, accounts, or identity concepts in the codebase — no authentication, authorization, session, cookie, or token handling exists — so every caller is treated identically and receives identical output.

**Geographic and market coverage.** Not applicable in any distributed sense. Coverage is a single machine's loopback interface. There is no multi-region deployment, no CDN, no load balancing, no DNS configuration, no internationalization or localization, and no timezone or currency handling. The single response body is fixed ASCII text with no locale variance.

**Data domains included.** One static string constitutes the entirety of the system's data.

| Data Element | Nature | Lifecycle |
|---|---|---|
| `Hello, World!` plus newline | Hardcoded response literal, 14 bytes | Compiled into source; never varies |
| `hostname`, `port` constants | Hardcoded configuration literals | Fixed at author time |
| Startup log line | Transient standard-output text | Emitted once at startup; not persisted |

No request data is read, parsed, stored, or logged. There is no database, no file I/O, no cache, no queue, and no in-memory state that survives a request. Accordingly, no personal data, regulated data, or business records are processed, and no data-retention, encryption, backup, or privacy-compliance concern arises from the code as written.

### 1.3.2 Out-of-Scope

#### 1.3.2.1 Excluded Application Capabilities

Each item below was confirmed absent by inspecting every file in the repository. The single `require` of Node's `http` module is the only import present, and no routing, error-handling, configuration, or security construct appears anywhere in the source.

| Excluded Capability | Confirmation |
|---|---|
| URL routing and method dispatch | The handler never reads the request object |
| Request body, query, or header processing | No parsing of any request input |
| Dynamic or templated responses | Single hardcoded literal response |
| Non-`200` status codes and error responses | Status is unconditionally `200` |
| Authentication, authorization, sessions | No credential, token, or identity handling |
| TLS / HTTPS | No `https` usage; plain HTTP only |
| Data persistence of any kind | No database, file, or cache access |
| Static asset or file serving | No file system reads; no `public/` directory |
| Runtime configuration | No `process.env` reference, `.env` file, or config loader |
| Error handling and resilience | No `try`/`catch`, no `'error'` listener |
| Graceful shutdown | No signal handlers; no `process.exit` |
| Timeout, keep-alive, or connection tuning | No timeout or socket settings in code |
| Rate limiting, CORS, compression, caching headers | No middleware layer of any kind |
| Observability instrumentation | No metrics, tracing, or logging framework |
| Clustering, worker threads, or multi-process scaling | Single-process script only |
| Off-host network exposure | Bind restricted to `127.0.0.1`, verified unreachable externally |

#### 1.3.2.2 Excluded Engineering Infrastructure

The following supporting infrastructure is absent from the repository. Each was checked individually.

| Category | Absent Artifacts |
|---|---|
| Automated testing | No `test/`, `tests/`, `__tests__/`, or `spec/` directory; no Jest or Mocha configuration; `npm test` exits 1 by design |
| Continuous integration / delivery | No `.github/` workflows, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`, `Makefile`, or `Procfile` |
| Containerization and orchestration | No `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose` file, or `.dockerignore` |
| Build and transpilation | No `tsconfig.json`, Babel, or bundler configuration; no `src/`, `lib/`, `dist/`, or `build/` directory |
| Code quality tooling | No ESLint, Prettier, or `.editorconfig` configuration |
| Runtime version pinning | No `engines` field, `.nvmrc`, or `.node-version` file |
| Environment and secrets management | No `.env`, `.env.example`, or `.npmrc` |

#### 1.3.2.3 Integration Points Not Covered

No integration beyond the in-process `http` module and standard output is implemented. Specifically excluded, all confirmed by the absence of any corresponding client, driver, or SDK in the dependency-free manifests: relational and NoSQL databases; message brokers and event streams; caches; third-party or internal REST, GraphQL, and gRPC APIs; identity providers and single sign-on; payment, email, and notification services; object storage; secret managers; service discovery and API gateways; feature-flag services; and APM or log-aggregation backends. The system makes no outbound network calls whatsoever.

It is worth restating the distinction drawn in section 1.2.1.3: the "backprop integration" named in the README is an integration performed **on** this repository by external tooling through Git and npm conventions. No code inside this repository participates in it, and implementing such code is out of scope.

#### 1.3.2.4 Unsupported Use Cases

Given the implementation, the following uses are not supported and would require changes the repository does not contain.

- **Serving traffic to remote clients.** The loopback bind makes off-host access impossible without a source change.
- **Production or shared-environment deployment.** No configurability, error handling, shutdown handling, health checks, observability, or deployment tooling exists.
- **Consumption as a reusable library.** `server.js` exports nothing, and the `main` field points to a non-existent `index.js`, so the package cannot be meaningfully imported.
- **Serving as a CI quality gate.** `npm test` fails by design, so any pipeline asserting a passing test suite will fail.
- **Concurrent instances on one host.** Two processes cannot both bind port 3000, and the resulting bind error is unhandled.
- **Any behavior conditional on request content.** The response is invariant by construction, so content-driven scenarios cannot be exercised.
- **Modification of the repository.** The README explicitly instructs that the project not be touched, which places changes to it outside the sanctioned scope.

#### 1.3.2.5 Future Phase Considerations

The repository documents **no** future phases. There is no roadmap, backlog, `TODO` or `FIXME` comment, milestone, changelog, issue template, or open branch: the history consists of a single commit on `main`, and the working tree is clean. Nothing in the codebase indicates planned work.

Only one latent inconsistency is visible that a future change could resolve — `package.json` names `index.js` as its `main` entry point while the implementation resides in `server.js` — and even that is recorded here as an observation, not as a recommendation. The README's "Do not touch!" directive weighs against any evolution of this artifact, and this specification treats the current content as the intended final state.

| Absence probes across ~40 conventional paths | Verified absence of CI/CD, containerization, tests, build tooling, linters, version pinning, env/secrets, extended docs, and alternate lockfiles (section 1.3.2.2) |
| Static search across all `.js`, `.json`, and `.md` files | Only two matches repository-wide (`require('http')` and `server.listen`), confirming no `process.env`, exports, routing, error handling, signal handling, TLS, or credential material exists |
| Git history inspection | Single commit `1a0874d` ("Add files via upload") added all four files; branch `main` only; no tags; clean working tree; no `.gitignore`; hosted as `28-july-existing-projects-qa-test-01` |
| Runtime execution and HTTP probing | Startup log string matched exactly; `GET /`, `POST /anything/else?q=1` with a body, and `DELETE /deep/path` all returned identical `200` / `text/plain` / 14-byte responses; loopback-only binding confirmed when the host's routable address refused connection; `npm test` confirmed to exit with code 1 |
| Response header attribution | `Content-Length`, `Date`, `Connection`, and `Keep-Alive` observed on the wire originate from Node.js `http` runtime defaults, not from repository configuration (section 1.2.2.3) |

### 1.4.4 External Sources

No external sources were used. One web lookup regarding Node.js release status was attempted and returned no usable result; consequently this section makes no claim about external Node.js versions, release schedules, or support windows. The only version-adjacent inference drawn is that `lockfileVersion: 3` corresponds to a modern npm lockfile format, stated in section 1.3.1.1 solely as a manifest-compatibility requirement.

No other sections of this Technical Specification were available for cross-reference at the time this Introduction was written; all content therefore derives directly from repository inspection. Forward references within this section point to material contained in it: section 1.2.1.3 (integration landscape), section 1.2.2.3 (technical approach and header attribution), section 1.3.1.1 (technical requirements), and section 1.3.2.2 (excluded engineering infrastructure).


# 2. Product Requirements

## 2.1 Feature Catalog

This catalog decomposes the repository into discrete, independently testable features. As established in section 1.1, the entire codebase is **four files and 39 lines** (913 bytes) at the repository root: `README.md`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, and `server.js`. The feature set is therefore small and completely enumerable — every capability the system possesses is catalogued below, and nothing is catalogued that is not present in those four files.

### 2.1.1 Catalog Derivation and Conventions

#### 2.1.1.1 Derivation Method

The repository contains no requirements document, product brief, backlog, issue templates, roadmap, or design notes — `README.md` is the only narrative artifact and it is two lines long. No requirement statements were therefore available to transcribe. Every feature and requirement in section 2 was **reverse-derived** from two evidence classes:

| Evidence Class | What It Provided | Where Applied |
|---|---|---|
| Static inspection | Exact source lines, manifest fields, and documented intent | Feature boundaries, metadata, dependencies |
| Runtime execution | Measured status codes, headers, payload byte counts, exit codes, log output | Acceptance criteria in section 2.2 |

Both classes are cited to specific file and line anchors throughout. Where a behavior originates from the Node.js or npm runtime rather than from repository code, that attribution is stated explicitly; this mirrors the header-attribution treatment in section 1.2.2.3.

#### 2.1.1.2 Identifier and Rating Conventions

| Convention | Format | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Feature identifier | `F-XXX` | Sequential, `F-001` through `F-007`; no gaps, no retired IDs |
| Requirement identifier | `F-XXX-RQ-YYY` | Scoped to its parent feature; assigned in section 2.2 |
| Known deviation identifier | `D-00X` | Documented anomalies, catalogued in section 2.2.9 |
| Priority (feature level) | Critical / High / Medium / Low | Ranked by whether the fixture's purpose survives the feature's removal |
| Priority (requirement level) | Must-Have / Should-Have / Could-Have | Assigned in section 2.2 |
| Status | Proposed / Approved / In Development / Completed | All seven features are **Completed** |

**Basis for the uniform Completed status.** All four files entered the repository in a single commit (`1a0874d`, "Add files via upload"), the working tree is clean, there are no tags, no additional branches, and no `TODO`/`FIXME` markers anywhere in the source. Section 1.3.2.5 further establishes that the repository documents no future phases and that the current content is the intended final state. Every feature below was additionally confirmed to function by direct execution. No feature is partially implemented.

Four categories organize the catalog. They correspond to the artifact boundaries that actually exist in the repository rather than to any layering declared by the project.

### 2.1.3 F-001: HTTP Listener Binding and Process Lifecycle

**Feature Metadata**

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Unique ID | F-001 |
| Feature Name | HTTP Listener Binding and Process Lifecycle |
| Feature Category | Runtime Service — Network Transport |
| Priority Level | Critical |
| Status | Completed |

**Description**

*Overview.* The feature opens a TCP listener for HTTP traffic on the loopback address `127.0.0.1` at port `3000` as the side effect of evaluating `server.js`. The bind parameters are declared as `const` literals on lines 3 and 4, the server object is created on line 6, and the bind is invoked on line 12. There is no configuration layer: a repository-wide search returned **zero** occurrences of `process.env`, and no `.env` file, `.npmrc`, or configuration module exists.

*Business Value.* This is the feature that makes the repository an exercisable target rather than a static code sample. Section 1.1.2 identifies the artifact's purpose as a known-good, zero-variance subject for an external integration named "backprop"; without a bound listener there is nothing for that tooling to exercise end to end.

*User Benefits.* Consumers get a launch path with no prerequisites — no install, build, transpile, or configuration step — and a bind target that is identical on every machine because it is hardcoded. The loopback restriction means exercising the fixture cannot inadvertently expose a network-facing surface, which was confirmed empirically: a request to the host's routable address (`10.76.1.16:3000`) was refused while `127.0.0.1:3000` served normally.

*Technical Context.* The only import in the repository is Node's built-in `http` module on line 1. The listener is created through `http.createServer(...)` and bound through `server.listen(port, hostname, callback)`. No `'error'` listener is registered and no `try`/`catch` exists, so bind failure is handled by Node's default unhandled-error path: a second concurrent instance produced `Error: listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use 127.0.0.1:3000` (errno −98, syscall `listen`) with a stack trace on stderr and process **exit code 1**. Likewise, no `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT` handler exists, so termination is immediate with no connection draining; the port is released by the operating system on exit.

**Dependencies**

| Dependency Class | Item | Nature |
|---|---|---|
| Prerequisite Features | None | F-001 is the root feature; it depends on no other catalogued feature |
| System Dependencies | Node.js runtime with CommonJS `require` and the `http` API | Mandatory; no `engines` field pins a version |
| System Dependencies | TCP port `3000` free on the loopback interface | Mandatory; contention is fatal and unhandled |
| External Dependencies | None | Zero third-party packages; no registry access needed at runtime |
| Integration Requirements | Inbound HTTP over the loopback interface only | The single integration surface of the whole system |

### 2.1.4 F-002: Invariant Fixed HTTP Response

**Feature Metadata**

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Unique ID | F-002 |
| Feature Name | Invariant Fixed HTTP Response |
| Feature Category | Runtime Service — Request Handling |
| Priority Level | Critical |
| Status | Completed |

**Description**

*Overview.* A single inline arrow function registered at `server.js` line 6 handles every accepted request. It performs exactly three statements — set status `200` (line 7), set `Content-Type: text/plain` (line 8), end the response with the 14-byte body `Hello, World!` plus a newline (line 9). The `req` parameter is accepted but never read; searches for `req.url`, `req.method`, `req.headers`, and `req.on` all returned zero matches.

*Business Value.* Invariance is the property that makes the repository useful as a fixture. Because the response cannot vary with client behavior, any deviation observed by consuming tooling isolates the fault to that tooling rather than to the subject — the reasoning set out in section 1.1.2.

*User Benefits.* Consumers can assert on an exact byte sequence rather than a schema. Verification confirmed a single response signature (`200` / 14 bytes / `text/plain`) across 50 sequential requests to 50 distinct paths and query strings, across 20 concurrent requests, and across the methods `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, and `OPTIONS` (identical body checksum in every case). Non-standard methods behave the same way: a `PURGE` request also returned `200` with 14 bytes.

*Technical Context.* Response construction is three statements:

```javascript
res.statusCode = 200;
res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/plain');
res.end('Hello, World!\n');
```

`Content-Type` is the only header set by repository code, and it carries no `charset` parameter. The `Date`, `Connection`, `Keep-Alive`, and `Content-Length` headers observed on the wire are Node.js `http` defaults, not repository configuration — the attribution established in section 1.2.2.3. The handler is stateless: no variable is mutated per request, and no persistence, cache, session, or file access exists anywhere in the codebase.

**Dependencies**

| Dependency Class | Item | Nature |
|---|---|---|
| Prerequisite Features | F-001 (HTTP Listener Binding) | Hard; the handler only executes for connections the listener accepts |
| System Dependencies | Node.js `http` response object (`statusCode`, `setHeader`, `end`) | Mandatory API surface |
| System Dependencies | Node.js default response framing headers | Supplies `Content-Length`, `Date`, `Connection`, `Keep-Alive` |
| External Dependencies | None | No template engine, serializer, or middleware |
| Integration Requirements | Any HTTP client capable of reaching the loopback interface | No client-side capability, header, or credential is required |

### 2.1.5 F-003: Startup Announcement Logging

**Feature Metadata**

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Unique ID | F-003 |
| Feature Name | Startup Announcement Logging |
| Feature Category | Operational Feedback |
| Priority Level | High |
| Status | Completed |

**Description**

*Overview.* The callback passed to `server.listen` writes one line to standard output once the listener is bound. The message is built with a template literal from the same `hostname` and `port` constants used for the bind (`server.js` line 13), so the announced URL cannot drift from the actual bind target.

*Business Value.* The line is the system's only readiness signal. For automation that must know when the fixture is serving, it is the sole in-band indicator available — there is no health endpoint distinguishable from the default response, no readiness probe, and no metrics or tracing instrumentation anywhere in the repository (section 1.2.3.3).

*User Benefits.* Operators and harnesses get an exact, greppable string to synchronize on. Byte-level verification confirmed standard output equals `Server running at http://127.0.0.1:3000/` followed by a newline, 41 bytes in total, with no prefix, timestamp, or log level.

*Technical Context.* Logging uses `console.log` directly; no logging library, log level, structured format, or output file is involved. The announcement is emitted exactly once and nothing else is ever written: after more than seventy requests, standard output still contained exactly one line. Because the write happens in the `listening` callback, the line is a genuine post-bind signal rather than an optimistic pre-bind message.

**Dependencies**

| Dependency Class | Item | Nature |
|---|---|---|
| Prerequisite Features | F-001 (HTTP Listener Binding) | Hard; the callback fires only after a successful bind |
| System Dependencies | Process standard output stream | Sole log sink |
| System Dependencies | `hostname` and `port` constants (`server.js` lines 3–4) | Shared with F-001; guarantees the announced URL matches the bind |
| External Dependencies | None | No logging framework or log shipper |
| Integration Requirements | A consumer that captures process stdout | Outbound, host-local only |

### 2.1.6 F-004: Package Identity and Manifest Declaration

**Feature Metadata**

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Unique ID | F-004 |
| Feature Name | Package Identity and Manifest Declaration |
| Feature Category | Packaging, Supply Chain, and Tooling |
| Priority Level | High |
| Status | Completed |

**Description**

*Overview.* `package.json` declares the repository as a well-formed npm package: name `hello_world`, version `1.0.0`, description "Hello world in Node.js", `main` `index.js`, a single `test` script, author `hxu`, and the MIT license. It declares neither `dependencies` nor `devDependencies`, and it omits `engines`, `type`, `private`, `repository`, and `files`.

*Business Value.* Conformance to npm conventions is precisely how the repository integrates with external tooling. Section 1.2.1.3 characterizes the "backprop" integration as ecosystem-level rather than code-level: the manifest is what lets that tooling clone, read, and optionally install the project through standard commands without any bespoke adapter.

*User Benefits.* Consumers obtain a stable, machine-readable identity (`hello_world@1.0.0`) and an unambiguous license declaration. Because `dependencies` is absent, install is a no-op and no registry availability assumption is introduced.

*Technical Context.* The manifest omits a `"type"` field, so Node treats `server.js` as CommonJS, matching its `require` usage. Two consequences of the declared fields are documented as deviations in section 2.2.9 rather than as behavior: `main` names `index.js`, which does not exist in the repository, so requiring the package root fails with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`; and no `start` script is declared, yet `npm start` still launches the server because npm supplies a built-in default of `node server.js` when a `server.js` file sits at the package root — behavior owned by the npm CLI, not by this repository.

**Dependencies**

| Dependency Class | Item | Nature |
|---|---|---|
| Prerequisite Features | None | The manifest stands alone |
| System Dependencies | JSON-parsing consumer (npm CLI or Node) | Mandatory for any manifest operation |
| External Dependencies | None declared | Zero `dependencies`, zero `devDependencies` |
| Integration Requirements | npm-compatible tooling reading `package.json` conventions | The ecosystem-level integration surface described in section 1.2.1.3 |
| Integration Requirements | Consistency with `package-lock.json` identity fields | Name, version, and license are duplicated in the lockfile |

### 2.1.7 F-005: Deterministic Zero-Dependency Resolution

**Feature Metadata**

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Unique ID | F-005 |
| Feature Name | Deterministic Zero-Dependency Resolution |
| Feature Category | Packaging, Supply Chain, and Tooling |
| Priority Level | Medium |
| Status | Completed |

**Description**

*Overview.* `package-lock.json` (`lockfileVersion: 3`, `requires: true`) contains a `packages` map holding **only** the root entry — name `hello_world`, version `1.0.0`, license MIT. No third-party package is locked, which is the machine-verifiable guarantee that the install graph is empty.

*Business Value.* Zero dependencies eliminate an entire class of failure that would otherwise contaminate integration runs: registry outages, resolution conflicts, transitive vulnerabilities, and version drift. Section 1.1.4 lists this as a primary value the artifact delivers.

*User Benefits.* Install is deterministic and offline-capable. `npm ci` completed with exit code 0, reported auditing a single package and zero vulnerabilities, and created **no** `node_modules` directory; `npm ls --all` reports an empty dependency tree beneath `hello_world@1.0.0`.

*Technical Context.* The lockfile's presence alongside an empty dependency set is a deliberate assertion rather than an omission: `npm ci` requires a lockfile, so shipping one lets consumers use the strict, reproducible install path and still get a no-op. `lockfileVersion: 3` requires an npm release that understands that format, which section 1.3.1.1 records as a manifest-compatibility requirement. No alternate lockfile (`yarn.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`) exists to contradict it.

**Dependencies**

| Dependency Class | Item | Nature |
|---|---|---|
| Prerequisite Features | F-004 (Package Identity) | Hard; the lockfile mirrors the manifest's name, version, and license |
| System Dependencies | npm CLI supporting `lockfileVersion: 3` | Mandatory for lockfile-driven installs |
| External Dependencies | None | No package registry access is required, since nothing is locked |
| Integration Requirements | Any `npm ci` or `npm install` step in consuming automation | Must tolerate a no-op install and the absence of `node_modules` |

### 2.1.9 F-007: Placeholder Test Script Contract

**Feature Metadata**

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Unique ID | F-007 |
| Feature Name | Placeholder Test Script Contract |
| Feature Category | Packaging, Supply Chain, and Tooling |
| Priority Level | Low |
| Status | Completed |

**Description**

*Overview.* The `scripts` map in `package.json` contains exactly one entry, `test`, whose command is `echo "Error: no test specified" && exit 1`. Invoking it prints the message and terminates with exit code 1, which was verified twice.

*Business Value.* The value is honesty of signal rather than verification: the repository contains no test suite — no `test/`, `tests/`, `__tests__/`, or `spec/` directory and no test-runner configuration — and the script says so unambiguously instead of exiting 0 and implying coverage that does not exist.

*User Benefits.* Consumers integrating this repository learn immediately that `npm test` is not a quality gate. Section 1.3.2.4 records "serving as a CI quality gate" as an explicitly unsupported use case for exactly this reason.

*Technical Context.* The command is the npm initializer's default placeholder, retained unchanged. It is a shell one-liner with no runner, no framework, and no dependency; its behavior is therefore stable across environments that provide `echo` and shell `exit`. Any automation that treats a non-zero `npm test` exit as failure will fail deterministically against this repository — a deviation catalogued as D-003 in section 2.2.9.

**Dependencies**

| Dependency Class | Item | Nature |
|---|---|---|
| Prerequisite Features | F-004 (Package Identity) | Hard; the script is declared inside `package.json` |
| System Dependencies | npm CLI script runner and a POSIX-style shell providing `echo` | Mandatory for invocation |
| External Dependencies | None | No test framework or runner is installed or declared |
| Integration Requirements | Consuming pipelines must tolerate exit code 1 from `npm test` | Otherwise the pipeline fails by design |


## 2.2 Functional Requirements Table

This subsection specifies twenty-three requirements across the seven catalogued features. Each requirement is stated so that it can be verified by an observer with no access to the source — every acceptance criterion below was actually executed against the running system or evaluated against repository state, and the criteria record what was measured rather than what would be desirable.

### 2.2.1 Requirement Specification Conventions

#### 2.2.1.1 Identification and Rating Scales

| Element | Scale or Format | Meaning in This Specification |
|---|---|---|
| Requirement ID | `F-XXX-RQ-YYY` | `YYY` numbered from `001` within each feature |
| Priority | Must-Have | Removal breaks the fixture contract that section 1.1.2 describes |
| Priority | Should-Have | Materially supports the contract but the fixture still functions without it |
| Priority | Could-Have | Emergent or incidental; not deliberately implemented |
| Complexity | High / Medium / Low | Implementation effort and reasoning burden |

#### 2.2.1.2 Uniform Complexity Rating

**Every requirement in this section is rated Low complexity.** This is a considered assessment, not an unfilled column. The complete implementation is 14 executable lines in a single file with zero dependencies, zero conditional branches, zero asynchronous chains beyond the two runtime callbacks, and no state. There is no algorithm, schema, concurrency control, or integration handshake anywhere in the repository that could justify a higher rating for any individual requirement.

#### 2.2.1.3 Treatment of Performance Criteria

The repository declares **no** performance targets, service-level objectives, throughput budgets, latency thresholds, timeouts, or rate limits — section 1.2.3.3 records this as a verified absence, and a repository-wide search confirmed zero occurrences of `setTimeout` or any keep-alive or socket-tuning setting. Consequently, the "Performance Criteria" entries below express **determinism and invariance properties that were measured**, not speed or capacity guarantees. Any latency or throughput objective for this system must be established by the consuming tooling; none can be sourced from this repository.

### 2.2.2 F-001 Requirements — HTTP Listener Binding and Process Lifecycle

**Requirement Details**

| Requirement ID | Description | Acceptance Criteria | Priority / Complexity |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-001-RQ-001 | On evaluation of `server.js`, the process must create an HTTP server and bind a listener to host `127.0.0.1` port `3000` | Running `node server.js` produces a listening socket that accepts a TCP connection on `127.0.0.1:3000`; a subsequent HTTP request returns a response | Must-Have / Low |
| F-001-RQ-002 | Listener reachability must be confined to the loopback interface | A request to the host's routable address on port 3000 fails to connect (observed: `curl` exit code 7, `http_code=000` against `10.76.1.16:3000`) while the same request to `127.0.0.1:3000` returns `200` | Must-Have / Low |
| F-001-RQ-003 | Bind parameters must originate solely from in-source constants, with no external configuration input | `hostname` and `port` are `const` literals at `server.js` lines 3–4; a repository-wide search yields zero matches for `process.env`; no `.env`, `.npmrc`, or config file exists | Must-Have / Low |
| F-001-RQ-004 | When port `3000` on the loopback interface is already bound, the process must terminate rather than continue in a non-serving state (as-built, emergent behavior) | A second instance emits `Error: listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use 127.0.0.1:3000` (errno −98, syscall `listen`) to stderr as an unhandled `'error'` event and exits with code 1 | Could-Have / Low |

**Technical Specifications**

| Requirement ID | Input Parameters | Output / Response | Performance Criteria and Data Requirements |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-001-RQ-001 | None at invocation; no CLI arguments, flags, or environment variables are read | A bound TCP listener plus the F-003 startup line | Bind completes during process start with no retry loop; no data is read or persisted |
| F-001-RQ-002 | None | Connection accepted on `127.0.0.1`; connection refused on every non-loopback interface | Isolation is absolute, not probabilistic — verified by connection refusal, not by timeout |
| F-001-RQ-003 | `hostname = '127.0.0.1'`, `port = 3000` (source literals) | Identical bind target on every host and every run | Configuration data set is exactly two literals; nothing is read from disk or environment |
| F-001-RQ-004 | Pre-existing listener on `127.0.0.1:3000` | Stack trace on stderr; process exit code 1; no partial service | Failure is immediate at bind time; no request is ever served by the failing process |

**Validation Rules**

| Requirement ID | Business Rules | Data Validation | Security and Compliance |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-001-RQ-001 | The listener is the fixture's only exercisable surface and must open unconditionally at startup | No input to validate; the bind takes no runtime parameters | Plain HTTP only; no TLS, certificate, or `https` usage exists in the repository |
| F-001-RQ-002 | Off-host exposure is out of scope per section 1.3.2.1 and must remain so | Not applicable | Loopback binding is the system's sole network control; there is no firewall rule, allowlist, or authentication layer |
| F-001-RQ-003 | Determinism requires that behavior cannot be altered by deployment environment | Literals are fixed at author time and require no validation | No secret, credential, or token is present in any file; nothing is sourced from the environment |
| F-001-RQ-004 | A conflicting bind must not yield a silently degraded fixture | Not applicable | The stack trace printed on failure exposes only the address, port, and syscall — no sensitive data |

### 2.2.3 F-002 Requirements — Invariant Fixed HTTP Response

**Requirement Details**

| Requirement ID | Description | Acceptance Criteria | Priority / Complexity |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-002-RQ-001 | Every accepted request must receive HTTP status `200`, irrespective of method, path, query string, headers, or body | `200` observed for `GET /`, `POST /anything/else?q=1` with a body, `DELETE /deep/path`, `HEAD /`, `OPTIONS /`, `PUT /`, `PATCH /`, and the non-standard method `PURGE /x` | Must-Have / Low |
| F-002-RQ-002 | The response must carry the header `Content-Type: text/plain` | Header present on every response; value is exactly `text/plain` with no `charset` parameter | Must-Have / Low |
| F-002-RQ-003 | The response body must be exactly `Hello, World!` followed by a single newline | Body measured at 14 bytes; byte sequence confirmed as `H e l l o ,` space `W o r l d !` `\n`; `Content-Length: 14` observed on the wire | Must-Have / Low |
| F-002-RQ-004 | The handler must not inspect the request; the response must be emitted in a single completion call | Searches for `req.url`, `req.method`, `req.headers`, and `req.on` return zero matches; the handler body is three statements ending in one `res.end(...)` | Must-Have / Low |
| F-002-RQ-005 | Response identity must hold across repeated and concurrent invocations | 50 sequential requests to 50 distinct paths and query strings produced exactly one distinct signature (`200` / 14 bytes / `text/plain`); 20 concurrent requests produced one signature; body checksum identical across six HTTP methods | Must-Have / Low |

**Technical Specifications**

| Requirement ID | Input Parameters | Output / Response | Performance Criteria and Data Requirements |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-002-RQ-001 | Any HTTP request line, headers, and body — all accepted, none evaluated | Status line `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` | No status varies under any input; there is no error, redirect, or 4xx/5xx path in the codebase |
| F-002-RQ-002 | None | `Content-Type: text/plain` set explicitly by `server.js` line 8 | The only header set by repository code; `Date`, `Connection`, `Keep-Alive`, and `Content-Length` come from Node defaults (section 1.2.2.3) |
| F-002-RQ-003 | None | 14-byte plain-text payload | Payload is a compiled-in string literal; no template, file read, or serialization occurs |
| F-002-RQ-004 | `req` object is bound but never dereferenced | Response completed with one `res.end` call; no chunked writes | Zero request data is parsed, buffered, stored, or logged |
| F-002-RQ-005 | Arbitrary request volume and concurrency | Byte-identical responses | Statelessness guarantees invariance: no per-request variable is mutated and no shared state exists |

**Validation Rules**

| Requirement ID | Business Rules | Data Validation | Security and Compliance |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-002-RQ-001 | Uniform success is the fixture contract; differentiated responses are out of scope per section 1.3.2.1 | No request validation is performed by design | No authentication, authorization, session, cookie, or token handling exists; all callers are anonymous and indistinguishable |
| F-002-RQ-002 | Content type must be stated explicitly rather than inferred by the client | Header value is a literal and needs no validation | `text/plain` avoids client-side interpretation of the payload as markup or script |
| F-002-RQ-003 | The payload must be assertable byte-for-byte by consuming tooling | Payload is a fixed literal; no encoding negotiation or locale variance | No personal, regulated, or business data is transmitted — the payload is a static greeting |
| F-002-RQ-004 | Input independence is what makes deviation attributable to the consumer | Deliberate non-validation of all request input | Not reading the request body eliminates deserialization, injection, and payload-size attack surface |
| F-002-RQ-005 | A fixture that varies under load cannot serve as a reference | Not applicable | Path traversal probes (for example `/../etc/passwd`) returned the same `200` / 14-byte response; no filesystem access occurs, since no `fs` usage exists anywhere |

### 2.2.4 F-003 Requirements — Startup Announcement Logging

**Requirement Details**

| Requirement ID | Description | Acceptance Criteria | Priority / Complexity |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-003-RQ-001 | Once the listener is bound, the process must write the line `Server running at http://127.0.0.1:3000/` to standard output | Standard output matches that string exactly, followed by a newline (41 bytes total, byte-verified), with no timestamp, level, or prefix | Must-Have / Low |
| F-003-RQ-002 | The announced URL must be derived from the same constants used to bind, so the message cannot diverge from reality | `server.js` line 13 interpolates `${hostname}` and `${port}` — the identical constants consumed by `server.listen` on line 12 | Should-Have / Low |
| F-003-RQ-003 | No further output may be produced during request handling or shutdown | Standard output still contained exactly one line after more than seventy requests; no output is emitted on `SIGTERM` termination | Should-Have / Low |

**Technical Specifications**

| Requirement ID | Input Parameters | Output / Response | Performance Criteria and Data Requirements |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-003-RQ-001 | Listener-bound event supplied by `server.listen`'s callback | One line on stdout, emitted exactly once per process | Emitted after bind completes, making it a true readiness signal rather than an optimistic message |
| F-003-RQ-002 | `hostname` and `port` constants | Interpolated URL `http://127.0.0.1:3000/` | Announced URL and bind target are provably identical because they share one source |
| F-003-RQ-003 | None | Silence for the remainder of process life | No request data reaches any log sink, so no request-derived data is retained anywhere |

**Validation Rules**

| Requirement ID | Business Rules | Data Validation | Security and Compliance |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-003-RQ-001 | This line is the only readiness indicator available; there is no health endpoint distinct from the default response | Not applicable | Discloses only the loopback address and port |
| F-003-RQ-002 | Operator-facing information must not contradict runtime behavior | Not applicable | No credential or environment detail is interpolated |
| F-003-RQ-003 | Log silence preserves the fixture's deterministic output signature | Not applicable | Absence of request logging means no client address, header, or payload is ever recorded |

| F-004-RQ-004 | The manifest must be valid, parseable JSON whose identity fields agree with the lockfile | File parses without error; `name`, `version`, and `license` match `package-lock.json` exactly; `npm ci` completes with exit code 0, which requires manifest/lockfile agreement | Must-Have / Low |

| Requirement ID | Input Parameters | Output / Response | Performance Criteria and Data Requirements |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-004-RQ-001 | None; the manifest is a static 251-byte document | Machine-readable identity `hello_world@1.0.0`, MIT-licensed | Data set is seven top-level keys; no nested structures beyond `scripts` |

**Validation Rules**

| Requirement ID | Business Rules | Data Validation | Security and Compliance |

| F-004-RQ-001 | npm-convention conformance is the integration mechanism described in section 1.2.1.3 | Fields are literal strings; no schema validation is performed by the repository | MIT license declared in the manifest; note that no `LICENSE` file accompanies it |
| F-004-RQ-002 | Tooling must be able to discover a test entry point even though no suite exists | Not applicable | The command executes only `echo` and `exit`; it touches no file and reads no input |
| F-004-RQ-003 | Zero dependencies is a stated value of the artifact (section 1.1.4) | Absence is itself the assertion | No transitive dependency can introduce a vulnerability; `npm ci` reported zero vulnerabilities |
| F-004-RQ-004 | Manifest and lockfile must not drift | JSON syntax validity is enforced by every consuming parser | Version consistency prevents ambiguity about which artifact is under test |

**Requirement Details**

| F-005-RQ-002 | A strict, lockfile-driven install must succeed without fetching any third-party package | `npm ci` exits 0, reports auditing one package and zero vulnerabilities, and creates no `node_modules` directory; the post-install file listing is unchanged | Must-Have / Low |
| F-005-RQ-003 | The lockfile root entry must mirror the manifest's identity | Lockfile root records `hello_world`, `1.0.0`, and `MIT`, matching `package.json` | Must-Have / Low |

| Requirement ID | Input Parameters | Output / Response | Performance Criteria and Data Requirements |
|---|---|---|---|

| F-005-RQ-002 | Lockfile plus manifest consumed by `npm ci` | Exit code 0 and an unchanged working tree | Install is offline-capable because no remote artifact is referenced |
| F-005-RQ-003 | None | Consistent identity across both manifests | Three duplicated fields must remain synchronized |

**Validation Rules**

| Requirement ID | Business Rules | Data Validation | Security and Compliance |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-005-RQ-001 | An empty but present lockfile is a deliberate assertion of a zero-dependency graph, enabling the strict install path | npm validates the lockfile format on read | `lockfileVersion: 3` requires a modern npm; older CLIs may not understand the format |
| F-005-RQ-002 | Install must never be a source of integration-run failure | npm reconciles the lockfile against the manifest and fails on mismatch | No supply-chain surface exists: nothing is downloaded, so no integrity hash or provenance check applies |
| F-005-RQ-003 | Duplicate identity data must agree between files | Compared by npm during install | Prevents ambiguity about the identity of the artifact under test |
