#### 6.6.4.4 Verification Activities Performed

All runtime verification was executed against the repository checkout with every scratch artifact written outside it under `/tmp`. The repository was never modified, and its unmodified state was re-confirmed afterwards: `git status --porcelain` empty, `git diff --stat` empty, `git ls-files` returning four paths, `HEAD` at `1a0874d`, no subdirectory present, `node_modules` absent, zero residual `node server.js` processes, and zero listeners on `127.0.0.1:3000`.

- **Test artifact absence probe.** Roughly eighty conventional testing, coverage, CI, hook, orchestration, runtime-pinning and security-tooling paths tested for existence; every one absent. Corroborated by semantic searches for test files and for test/CI/QA folders, both of which returned no results.
- **Static census of testing and security vocabulary.** Zero matches across all four tracked files for `describe(`, `it(`, `test(`, `assert`, `expect(`, `node:test`, `jest`, `mocha`, `chai`, `sinon`, `nock`, `msw`, `supertest`, `playwright`, `cypress`, `selenium`, `puppeteer`, `k6`, `artillery`, `autocannon`, `coverage`, `nyc`, `c8`, `lint`, `eslint`, `prettier`, `audit`, `workflow`, `dependencies`, `devDependencies`, `engines`, `module.exports`, `exports`, and for every security token searched (`authorization`, `token`, `password`, `secret`, `apiKey`, `api_key`, `credential`, `https`, `tls`, `ssl`, `cert`, `cors`, `helmet`, `csrf`, `sanitize`, `validate`, `escape`). The only test-related string in the repository is `scripts.test` on line 7 of `package.json`.
- **Declared test command execution.** `npm test` printed `> hello_world@1.0.0 test`, echoed `Error: no test specified`, and exited 1.
- **Framework availability check.** `require('node:test')` and `require('node:assert')` both resolved to functions on Node.js v22.23.1, and `node --test` is available, establishing a zero-installation framework option.
- **Startup and readiness measurement.** `node server.js` emitted exactly `Server running at http://127.0.0.1:3000/` plus a newline — 41 bytes verified with `od -c` — with empty stderr, and stdout remained exactly one line after the full request sweep. Boot to first stdout byte measured at 31.1 ms.
- **Twenty-one-case invariance matrix.** Seven methods (`GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS`, and the non-standard `PURGE`) across three paths (`/`, `/health`, `/deep/path?x=1`); every case returned `200`, 14 bytes and `text/plain` with an identical body checksum. The full header block on `GET /` was `Content-Type: text/plain`, `Date`, `Connection: keep-alive`, `Keep-Alive: timeout=5`, and `Content-Length: 14`.
- **Out-of-tree suite execution.** A `node:test` suite located outside the repository, spawning `node server.js` via `child_process.spawn`, asserting the exact banner and asserting `200`/`text/plain`/`Hello, World!\n` across `GET`, `POST` and `DELETE`, reported `# pass 2`, `# fail 0` with `duration_ms` of roughly 85 ms, with zero packages installed.
- **Coverage instrumentation limits.** `node --test --experimental-test-coverage` attributed 100% line, branch and function coverage to the suite file only, with `server.js` absent from the report. `NODE_V8_COVERAGE` produced zero coverage artifacts when the fixture was terminated by `SIGTERM` and again by `SIGINT`, while a control run against a cleanly exiting script produced one artifact.
- **Reporter verification.** The built-in `spec`, `tap`, `dot` and `junit` reporters were each exercised against the suite and each produced output, with `junit` emitting XML terminating in `</testsuites>`. The flags `--test-concurrency`, `--test-shard`, `--test-name-pattern`, `--test-force-exit` and `--test-reporter-destination` were confirmed available on the verified runtime.
- **Parallelism and fault verification.** A second `node server.js` launched while the first held the port exited 1 with an uncaught error containing `EADDRINUSE`, "address already in use", and `code: 'EADDRINUSE'`.
- **Network confinement verification.** A request to the host's routable address `10.76.1.16:3000` failed to connect (`http_code` 000, `curl` exit 7) while `127.0.0.1:3000` returned `200`.
- **Security and supply-chain verification.** `npm audit` reported "found 0 vulnerabilities" with exit 0; `npm ci` reported "up to date, audited 1 package in 137 ms" and created no `node_modules`, with a measured wall time of 0.186 s. A negative-input probe carrying a roughly 20,000-byte header returned **431** while stdout remained at 41 bytes, proving the response was runtime-generated and the handler was never invoked. Raw-socket malformed-request probing was not possible because `nc` is not installed in the verification environment.
- **Resource measurement.** Fixture resident set size measured at 51,616 kB and 58,644 kB across two runs, with a virtual reservation of 1,013,948 kB. Loopback latency over 200 sequential requests with a fresh connection each: p50 0.20 ms, p95 0.62 ms, p99 1.27 ms, max 6.25 ms.
- **Diagram render validation.** All three Mermaid diagrams in this section were rendered to SVG with mermaid-cli 11.16.0 before inclusion, each returning a zero exit status, and were audited for balanced `subgraph`/`end` pairs (5/5, 4/4 and 5/5 respectively) and for the absence of any edge originating from or terminating on a subgraph identifier.

#### 6.6.4.5 External Sources

No external or web sources were required for this section. Every statement is grounded in the repository's four tracked files, in direct measurement of the unmodified checkout with all scratch artifacts written outside it, or in the cross-referenced sections of this specification listed above.


# 7. User Interface Design

## 7.1 User Interface Determination

**No user interface required.**

This repository defines no user interface of any kind. The determination is not an inference drawn from a missing design document — it is the result of an exhaustive census of every file in the repository, a set of content-level marker sweeps, an inspection of the complete Git history, and direct runtime probing of the running process. Because the whole project is four files totalling 39 lines, the census is complete rather than sampled, and the absence can be asserted rather than assumed.

The sub-sections below record the evidence for that determination, identify what occupies the place a user interface would normally hold, and address each topic the User Interface Design scope enumerates with its measured disposition. No screen, view, template, component, stylesheet, or design asset is documented anywhere in this section, because none exists to document.

### 7.1.1 Basis for the Determination

Five independent lines of evidence were gathered. All five agree.

| Line of Evidence | Method | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Complete file census | Recursive listing of the checkout excluding `.git` | Exactly **4 files, 0 subdirectories**: `server.js`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `README.md`. No `public/`, `static/`, `views/`, `templates/`, `src/`, `client/`, `web/`, `assets/`, or `components/` directory exists |
| UI asset extension sweep | Filename sweep across the whole checkout for 22 presentation-layer extensions | **Zero matches** for `*.html`, `*.htm`, `*.css`, `*.scss`, `*.sass`, `*.less`, `*.jsx`, `*.tsx`, `*.vue`, `*.svelte`, `*.ejs`, `*.pug`, `*.hbs`, `*.handlebars`, `*.mustache`, `*.twig`, `*.png`, `*.jpg`, `*.svg`, `*.ico`, `*.woff*`, `*.ttf` — no markup, no stylesheet, no component file, no template, no image, no icon, no web font |
| Content marker sweeps | Case-insensitive greps across all four tracked files in five categories | **Zero matches** in every category (detailed in 7.1.2 below) |
| Git history | `git log --all --diff-filter=A --name-only` on the single-commit baseline `1a0874d` | The only paths ever tracked are the same four files — **no UI asset ever existed and none was removed** |
| Semantic repository index | Natural-language searches for frontend screens, templates, stylesheets, and browser-facing application code | Both file-level and folder-level searches returned **empty result sets** |

The dependency graph independently forecloses the possibility of a UI stack arriving transitively. `package.json` declares neither `dependencies` nor `devDependencies`, and `package-lock.json` (`lockfileVersion: 3`) contains exactly one entry in its `packages` map — the root package record — so no UI framework, bundler, transpiler, CSS toolchain, or icon library is present or resolvable.

```json
{ "name": "hello_world", "version": "1.0.0", "lockfileVersion": 3,
  "requires": true, "packages": { "": { "name": "hello_world", "version": "1.0.0", "license": "MIT" } } }
```
*The entirety of `package-lock.json` — one root record, zero installed packages.*

### 7.1.2 UI Technology Categories Probed and Found Absent

Every marker below was searched for case-insensitively across all four tracked files and returned zero matches. The categories were chosen to cover every mainstream way a user interface can be delivered.

| Delivery Model | Markers Probed | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Client-side SPA frameworks | `react`, `vue`, `angular`, `svelte`, `next`, `nuxt`, `ember`, `backbone`, `jquery` | Absent |
| Build and asset tooling | `webpack`, `vite`, `rollup`, `parcel`, `babel` | Absent |
| Styling and design systems | `tailwind`, `bootstrap`, `material`, plus all CSS/SCSS/LESS file extensions | Absent |
| Server-rendered views | `express`, `koa`, `fastify`, `hapi`, `nest`, `ejs`, `pug`, `jade`, `handlebars`, `hbs`, `mustache`, `nunjucks`, `view engine` | Absent |
| Static file and asset serving | `sendFile`, `serve-static`, `readFileSync`, `__dirname` | Absent |
| Browser/DOM APIs and markup | `text/html`, `<html`, `<!doctype`, `<body`, `<div`, `document.`, `window.`, `innerHTML`, `querySelector`, `render(` | Absent |
| Real-time UI transports | `socket.io`, `websocket`, `ws://` | Absent |
| Interactive API consoles | `swagger`, `openapi`, `redoc`, `graphql`, `graphiql` | Absent |
| Command-line and terminal UIs | `commander`, `yargs`, `inquirer`, `chalk`, `blessed`, `ink`, `prompt`, `readline`, `process.argv`, `process.stdin` | Absent |
| Desktop and mobile shells | `electron`, `tauri`, `nw.js`, `react-native`, `flutter`, `qt`, `gtk`, `tkinter`, `webview` | Absent |

Section 3.2.6 of this specification reaches the same conclusion from the technology-selection perspective, recording React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, jQuery, Tailwind, Electron, React Native, and Next.js as probed and absent, and stating explicitly that a conventional React/TypeScript/Tailwind web stack "is **not** present in this repository". Section 1.3.2.1 records "Dynamic or templated responses" and "Static asset or file serving" as excluded capabilities, noting that there are no filesystem reads and no `public/` directory. Section 3.2.3 records that the role normally filled by a templating or serialisation library is filled by "Nothing — a string literal is passed to `res.end`".

The absence of a command-line interface deserves a specific note, because a CLI is the interface model a small Node.js script would most plausibly have adopted. `server.js` contains no argument parsing (`process.argv` has zero occurrences), no interactive prompting, no `readline` usage, and no help or usage text. `package.json` declares no `bin` field, so the package installs no executable, and its only script is a deliberately failing placeholder (`echo "Error: no test specified" && exit 1`). Standard output is written exactly once, at startup, as a readiness line — not as an interactive display.

### 7.1.3 Interface Category Adjudication

Each recognised user-interface category was adjudicated against the repository. All resolve negative.

| Interface Category | Verdict | Decisive Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Web application (client-rendered) | **Not present** | No HTML entry document, no JavaScript bundle, no component files, no bundler configuration, and no dependency graph in which a framework could sit |
| Web application (server-rendered) | **Not present** | No view engine, no template file, and no code path that composes markup; the response body is a compiled-in string literal at `server.js` line 9 |
| Static site or documentation site | **Not present** | No static assets exist and the process performs no filesystem I/O, so no file can be served |
| Administrative or internal console | **Not present** | No routes, no forms, no authentication, and no identity concept — section 1.3.1.2 records "no roles, permissions, tenants, accounts, or identity concepts in the codebase" |
| Interactive API explorer (Swagger UI, Redoc, GraphiQL) | **Not present** | Section 6.3.2.8 records no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL SDL, JSON Schema, or request-collection artifact of any kind |
| Command-line or terminal interface | **Not present** | No `bin` entry, no argument parsing, no prompting library, no TUI library; stdout carries one readiness line per process lifetime |
| Desktop application | **Not present** | No Electron, Tauri, or native toolkit marker; no window, menu, or tray construct |
| Mobile application | **Not present** | No React Native, Flutter, or native mobile project structure |
| Notebook or dashboard surface | **Not present** | No notebook files, no charting library, no dashboard definition |
| Email, PDF, or other rendered output | **Not present** | No template, renderer, or document-generation code; the only output artefact is a 14-byte plain-text body |

### 7.1.4 What Occupies the Place of a User Interface

The system's entire externally reachable surface is a single HTTP listener bound to the loopback interface, plus the process's standard output. There is no presentation tier above it and no client artefact shipped with it. The consumer named in `README.md` line 2 — "test project for backprop integration" — interacts with the system programmatically, and section 6.3.4.1 records that relationship as inbound and one-directional: the tooling calls the fixture, and nothing in `server.js` is aware of the tooling's existence.

```javascript
res.statusCode = 200;
res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/plain');
res.end('Hello, World!\n');
```
*`server.js` lines 7–9 — the complete response-producing logic. `Content-Type` is the only header set by repository code, and the body is a 14-byte literal.*

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    CONSUMER["Host-local HTTP consumer<br/>curl, an HTTP client library,<br/>or the backprop test tooling"]

    subgraph ServiceTier["Service Tier - the entire implemented system"]
        LISTEN["TCP listener 127.0.0.1:3000<br/>server.js L3-L4 and L12"]
        RUNTIME["Node.js core http runtime<br/>parse, dispatch, frame, serialize"]
        HANDLER["Single inline request listener<br/>200, text-plain, 14 bytes<br/>server.js L6-L10"]
        STDOUT["Standard output<br/>one readiness line<br/>server.js L13"]
        LISTEN --> RUNTIME
        RUNTIME --> HANDLER
        HANDLER --> RUNTIME
        HANDLER -.-> STDOUT
    end

    subgraph AbsentPresentation["Presentation Tier - probed for and verified absent"]
        DOCSHELL["HTML document or application shell"]
        COMPONENTS["Component tree or view templates"]
        STYLES["Stylesheets, design tokens, web fonts"]
        CLIENTSTATE["Client-side state store and router"]
        MEDIA["Images, icons, favicon"]
    end

    CONSUMER -->|"HTTP request over loopback<br/>method, path, headers and body all ignored"| LISTEN
    RUNTIME -->|"Hello, World! plus newline"| CONSUMER
    HANDLER -.->|"no markup is ever emitted"| DOCSHELL
    HANDLER -.-> COMPONENTS
    HANDLER -.-> STYLES
    HANDLER -.-> CLIENTSTATE
    HANDLER -.-> MEDIA
```

*Diagram 7.1.4-A — The consumer boundary. Solid edges are measured data paths; every node in the lower subgraph was probed for and found absent, and the dotted edges represent relationships that do not exist.*

### 7.1.5 Browser Access Does Not Constitute a User Interface

Because the system speaks HTTP on a port a browser can address, it is worth recording precisely what a browser receives, so that reachability is not mistaken for a user interface. The following was measured against the running process (Node.js v22.23.1) using a browser-shaped request — Chrome `User-Agent`, `Accept: text/html,application/xhtml+xml,...`, and `Accept-Language: en-US,en;q=0.9`.

```text
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/plain
Content-Length: 14
```
*Measured response to a browser-shaped `GET /`. The `Accept` preference for HTML is ignored; `text/plain` is the only content type the application ever sets, and it carries no `charset` parameter.*

| Browser Behaviour | Measured Outcome | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Content negotiation for HTML | `Accept: text/html,...` ignored; response is `text/plain` with no `Vary` header | No document is delivered, so **no DOM is ever constructed**; the browser displays raw text |
| Request for the document root | `GET /` → `200`, `text/plain`, 14 bytes (`Hello, World!` plus newline, confirmed byte-for-byte) | There is nothing to bootstrap an application from |
| Request for an entry document | `GET /index.html` → `200`, `text/plain`, 14 bytes | The greeting is returned instead of markup |
| Request for a script bundle | `GET /app.js` → `200`, `text/plain`, 14 bytes | No client-side code can be loaded |
| Request for a stylesheet | `GET /styles.css` and `GET /static/app.css` → `200`, `text/plain`, 14 bytes | No styling can be loaded |
| Request for a favicon or image | `GET /favicon.ico` and `GET /assets/logo.svg` → `200`, `text/plain`, 14 bytes | No icon or image asset can be loaded |
| Cross-origin access from a hosted UI | No `Access-Control-*` header is ever emitted (section 6.3.2.2.5) | A browser-based UI served from any other origin could not read the response |
| Live-updating UI over WebSocket | `Upgrade: websocket` and `Upgrade: h2c` both receive an ordinary `200`; **no `101 Switching Protocols` is ever emitted** (section 6.3.2.2.6) | No push- or socket-driven interface is possible |
| Localised presentation | `Accept-Language` ignored; section 1.3.1.2 records "no internationalization or localization" and a fixed ASCII body | The single rendered string cannot vary by locale |

Not one of the seven asset-style paths probed returned a response containing a single `<` character. Every path in the URI space yields the identical plain-text greeting, which is consistent with the finding in section 6.3.2.2.4 that no path is ever parsed. A browser pointed at `http://127.0.0.1:3000/` therefore acts as a plain-text viewer of a fixed payload, not as a client of an application interface.

### 7.1.6 Disposition of Each Prescribed User Interface Topic

The User Interface Design scope enumerates seven topics. Each is recorded below with its measured disposition, so that the "no user interface required" determination is explicit at the level of every individual requirement rather than only in aggregate.

| Prescribed Topic | Disposition |
|---|---|
| **Core UI technologies** | **None.** The repository declares zero dependencies and imports exactly one module — Node's core `http` — at `server.js` line 1. Section 3.2 establishes that the Node.js standard library is the entire framework layer, and section 3.2.6 records every front-end, CSS, desktop, and mobile technology as probed and absent |
| **UI use cases** | **None.** There is no interface through which a use case could be performed. The only workflows the repository supports are programmatic: launch the process, issue an HTTP request, resolve the (empty) dependency graph, and invoke the failing `test` script — enumerated as such in section 1.3.1.1 |
| **UI / backend interaction boundaries** | **Not applicable — there is no UI tier, so there is no UI-to-backend boundary.** The only boundary that exists is between an arbitrary HTTP consumer and the service, and it is documented in full in section 6.3.2: cleartext HTTP/1.1 on `127.0.0.1:3000`, one implicit endpoint covering the entire URI space, no authentication, no authorization, no rate limiting, no versioning, and no machine-readable contract. Section 6.3.5.2 additionally records that there is "no interception point" — one inline handler, no middleware chain, and no exports — so no presentation layer could be attached without editing `server.js` |
| **UI schemas** | **None.** No form schema, view model, validation schema, DTO, or type definition exists. There is no TypeScript, no `types`/`typings` field, and no schema-validation library (`zod`, `joi`, `ajv`, `yup` are all absent per section 6.3.2.8). The only data the system holds is a single hardcoded 14-byte string literal, which section 1.3.1.2 records as the entirety of its data domain |
| **Screens required** | **None. No UI screen exists in the repository.** The complete file census returned four files — `server.js`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `README.md` — none of which is a screen, page, view, layout, or component. The extension sweep found no markup or component file, and the Git history confirms none ever existed. There is consequently no screen to reference, no navigation map to draw, and no screen inventory to tabulate |
| **User interactions** | **None.** No event handler, input control, gesture, keyboard binding, or focus behaviour exists. The request object is bound as a handler parameter at `server.js` line 6 and never dereferenced, so the system cannot react to anything a user supplies: section 6.3.2.2.4 records that method, path, query string, headers, and body are all ignored, and section 6.3.2.5 records that no server-side trace of any interaction is retained — after 60 distinct requests, standard output still contained exactly one line |
| **Visual design considerations** | **None.** There is no layout, typography, colour system, spacing scale, design token, theme, dark mode, icon set, or web font. Nor is there any accessibility surface to consider: with no markup emitted, there is no semantic structure, no ARIA attribute, no focus order, and no contrast ratio to assess. Responsive behaviour is equally inapplicable, since no viewport-dependent rendering occurs |

### 7.1.7 Structural Constraints on Any Future User Interface

These are not recommendations. They are constraints that follow from the code as it exists, and each would have to be resolved before any user interface could be introduced. They are recorded so that the "no user interface required" determination is understood as a property of the design rather than an oversight.

| Constraint | Mechanism | Consequence for Any UI Work |
|---|---|---|
| Change freeze | `README.md` line 2 states "Do not touch!", recorded elsewhere in this specification as constraint C-001 | Adding any interface requires editing tracked content, which the directive prohibits; the constraint is governance rather than technique |
| Loopback confinement | `hostname = '127.0.0.1'` is compiled into `server.js` line 3 (constraint C-002); a request to the host's routable address is refused | A browser or client application on any other machine cannot reach the service at all, so no remotely served interface is possible without a source edit |
| Single invariant response | `server.js` lines 7–9 set `200`, `text/plain`, and a 14-byte literal unconditionally, with no routing code anywhere | A UI needs differentiated resources — a document, a script, a stylesheet, an API response. All of them would return the same greeting until routing were written |
| No content negotiation | `Accept` and `Accept-Language` are ignored and no `Vary` header is emitted | `text/html` cannot be requested; the server has no branch on which to emit markup |
| No filesystem access | Zero occurrences of `fs.`, `readFile`, `createReadStream`, `path.`, or `__dirname` | Static assets could not be served even if they were added to the repository |
| No interception point | One inline handler, no middleware chain, and no `module.exports` in `server.js` | View rendering, session handling, or asset middleware cannot be wrapped around the handler; they would have to be written into it |
| Empty install graph | `package-lock.json` locks only the root record; `npm ci` creates no `node_modules` | Any framework, bundler, or component library would require adding a dependency, re-locking, and accepting a network install — reversing the zero-dependency property |
| No cross-origin allowance | No `Access-Control-*` header is ever emitted | A separately hosted UI could not consume the endpoint from a browser |
| No upgrade path for live UIs | `Upgrade: websocket` and `h2c` receive an ordinary `200`; no `101` is ever emitted | Push-driven or collaborative interfaces are precluded without a source change |


## 7.2 References

### 7.2.1 Repository Files Examined

All four tracked files were read in full; the repository contains no others.

- `server.js` — the sole executable artifact. Established the complete response-producing logic (`res.statusCode = 200`, `res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/plain')`, `res.end('Hello, World!\n')` on lines 7–9), the single `require('http')` on line 1, the hardcoded loopback host and port on lines 3–4, the single inline request listener on lines 6–10 in which `req` is never dereferenced, and the readiness log on lines 12–14. Established by what it lacks: no markup generation, no template rendering, no static-file serving, no routing, no content negotiation, no filesystem access, no `module.exports`, and no interception point at which a presentation layer could be attached.
- `package.json` — established zero `dependencies` and zero `devDependencies`, the absence of any `bin` entry (so the package installs no executable and therefore no CLI), the absence of `browser`/`browserslist` fields, the absence of any build, start, or dev script, and a single deliberately failing `test` placeholder. Confirms that no UI framework, bundler, or design-system dependency is declared.
- `package-lock.json` — established `lockfileVersion: 3` with exactly one entry in `packages` (the root record), proving an empty install graph through which no UI framework, CSS toolchain, component library, or icon set could arrive transitively.
- `README.md` — established the project's stated purpose ("test project for backprop integration") and the "Do not touch!" change-freeze directive. Established by omission: no usage instructions, no screenshots, no interface documentation, and no reference to any client application.

### 7.2.2 Repository Folders Examined

- Repository root (`""`) — established by exhaustive recursive listing that the project comprises exactly four files and **zero subdirectories**. Confirmed the absence of every directory in which interface source would conventionally reside: `public/`, `static/`, `views/`, `templates/`, `src/`, `client/`, `web/`, `assets/`, `components/`, `pages/`, `styles/`, and `docs/`. Because the listing is complete rather than sampled, it is the decisive evidence that no screen or view artefact exists.

### 7.2.3 Technical Specification Sections Cross-Referenced

- `1.3 Scope` — corroborated that "Dynamic or templated responses" and "Static asset or file serving" are explicitly excluded capabilities with no filesystem reads and no `public/` directory; that exactly one undifferentiated user group exists ("no roles, permissions, tenants, accounts, or identity concepts in the codebase"); that no bundler, transpiler, `src/`, `dist/`, or `docs/` artefact exists; and that there is "no internationalization or localization", the response body being fixed ASCII with no locale variance.
- `3.2 Frameworks and Libraries` — corroborated that the repository uses no application framework and no third-party library, that the Node.js standard library is the entire framework layer (a seven-call surface), that templating and response serialisation are filled by "Nothing — a string literal is passed to `res.end`", and — in section 3.2.6 — that React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, jQuery, Tailwind, Next.js, Electron, and React Native were all probed and found absent, with an explicit statement that a conventional React/TypeScript/Tailwind web stack is not present.
- `6.3 Integration Architecture` — corroborated the complete consumer-boundary contract used in place of a UI/backend boundary: cleartext HTTP/1.1 on `127.0.0.1:3000` with one implicit endpoint over the whole URI space; `Accept` and `Accept-Language` ignored with no `Vary`; no `Access-Control-*` header ever emitted; `Upgrade: websocket` and `h2c` answered with an ordinary `200` and never a `101`; no OpenAPI, Swagger UI, Redoc, GraphQL, or schema-validation artifact; no server-side trace of interactions; and the "no interception point" finding (one inline handler, no middleware chain, no exports) together with constraints C-001 (change freeze) and C-002 (loopback confinement).

### 7.2.4 Verification Activities Performed

- **Complete file census** — recursive listing of the checkout excluding `.git`, returning four files and zero subdirectories, plus a hidden-entry check confirming `.git/` is the only hidden path.
- **UI asset extension sweep** — filename sweep across the whole checkout for 22 presentation-layer extensions (markup, stylesheets, component files, template files, images, icons, web fonts): zero matches.
- **Content marker sweeps** — case-insensitive greps across all four tracked files in five categories (markup and DOM APIs; front-end frameworks and bundlers; server frameworks, view engines, and static serving; real-time transports, API-doc consoles, and CLI/TUI libraries; desktop and mobile shells): zero matches in every category.
- **Routing and header census of `server.js`** — greps for `req.url`, `req.method`, `req.headers`, `switch`, and conditional statements returned no routing logic; the only `setHeader` call sets `Content-Type: text/plain`.
- **Git history inspection** — `git log --all --oneline --name-status` and `git log --all --diff-filter=A --name-only` against the single-commit baseline `1a0874d26682e67dac744b29b198b666cf39c126` on branch `main`, confirming the four tracked files are the only paths ever added and that no UI asset was ever present or removed. No tags exist.
- **Semantic index searches** — a file-level search for frontend page templates, screens, and client-side interface components, and a folder-level search for directories containing views, stylesheets, static assets, or browser-facing application code: both returned empty result sets.
- **Runtime browser-simulation probe** — the server was started and issued a request carrying a Chrome `User-Agent`, `Accept: text/html,application/xhtml+xml,application/xml;q=0.9,image/avif,image/webp,*/*;q=0.8`, and `Accept-Language: en-US,en;q=0.9`. The response was `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` with `Content-Type: text/plain` and `Content-Length: 14`, establishing that HTML is never negotiated.
- **Asset-path probe matrix** — `/`, `/index.html`, `/app.js`, `/styles.css`, `/static/app.css`, `/favicon.ico`, and `/assets/logo.svg` were each requested; all returned `200`, `text/plain`, and 14 bytes, with zero `<` characters in any body — establishing that no document, script, stylesheet, icon, or image can be obtained.
- **Response payload verification** — the body was dumped with `od -c` and confirmed byte-for-byte as `Hello, World!` plus a newline (exactly 14 bytes); a `HEAD` request confirmed `Content-Type` is the only application-set header, all others being Node.js runtime framing headers.
- **Verification environment** — Node.js v22.23.1. The repository declares no runtime version, so this is an environment fact rather than a repository requirement. `git status --porcelain` was empty both before and after all probing, so the tracked checkout was left byte-identical, honouring the `README.md` change freeze.
- **Ignore-file compliance** — a filesystem search for `.blitzyignore` files returned no results, so no path exclusions applied to this investigation.

### 7.2.5 External Sources

No external source was consulted for this section. Every statement is grounded in the repository files listed above, in the cross-referenced specification sections, or in the runtime measurements recorded in 7.2.4.


# 8. Infrastructure

## 8.1 Deployment Environment

**Detailed Infrastructure Architecture is not applicable for this system.**

This repository is a standalone, single-file Node.js HTTP sample that is executed directly on a developer or automation host. It provisions nothing, is deployed nowhere, and contains no artefact of any kind from which infrastructure could be derived. The determination is not an omission in the documentation — it is a measurable property of the repository, established by the four tests below.

| Applicability test | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Does the repository contain deployment or provisioning artefacts? | No — zero, in any class | `git ls-files` returns exactly four files (`README.md`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `server.js`) and the tree contains **no subdirectories at all**, so there is literally no directory in which infrastructure code could reside |
| Can the service be reached by any component outside its own host? | No | `server.js` line 3 binds the literal `127.0.0.1`; a probe against the host's own routable address on port 3000 was refused (`curl` exit 7, HTTP code `000`) — constraint **C-002** |
| Is there any surface through which an environment could be configured? | No | Content grep across all four tracked files finds no `process.env` and no `process.argv`; the bind address and port are source literals at `server.js` lines 3–4 — constraint **C-003** |
| May infrastructure be added to the repository? | No | `README.md` line 2 states the project must not be modified — constraint **C-001**; any Dockerfile, workflow, or manifest added would violate it and invalidate requirement **F-006-RQ-003** |

Scope of this determination and structure of Section 8:

- Sub-sections **8.2 Cloud Services**, **8.3 Containerization**, and **8.4 Orchestration** record evidence-backed *not-applicable* determinations, as the section prompt directs, rather than being omitted.
- Sub-sections **8.1**, **8.5 CI/CD Pipeline**, and **8.6 Infrastructure Monitoring** document what genuinely exists: a single-host execution environment, a source-to-run path with no build stage, and the one line of telemetry the process emits.
- Every figure quoted below is either a repository fact from a tracked file, a measurement executed against a disposable copy of the repository (the checkout itself was verified clean afterwards, honouring **C-001**), or an explicit cross-reference to an already-published specification section. Measurements taken from the verification host are labelled as environment observations, because the repository declares no runtime version (**D-005**).

### 8.1.1 Target Environment Assessment

#### 8.1.1.1 Environment Type

The target environment is **a single host, executing a single process, reachable only from that host**. It is not an on-premises tier, not a cloud environment, not hybrid, and not multi-cloud — none of those categories has any representation in the repository.

| Environment characteristic | Determination | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Environment type | Single-host local execution (developer workstation or automation runner) | The only executable artefact is `server.js`, launched as `node server.js`; §3.6.7 records the host OS as unconstrained |
| On-premises infrastructure | Not applicable | No inventory, host list, provisioning script, or systemd unit exists (`*.service`, `*.sh`, `Makefile*` all absent) |
| Cloud environment | Not applicable | No provider SDK in `package.json`, no provider configuration file, no cloud endpoint anywhere in the tree (see 8.2) |
| Hybrid or multi-cloud | Not applicable | Requires at least two environments; exactly one exists, and it has no network reach beyond loopback (**C-002**) |
| Number of concurrent instances supported | Exactly one per host | A second `node server.js` while port 3000 is bound raises an unhandled `'error'` event, `Error: listen EADDRINUSE`, `errno -98`, `syscall 'listen'`, and exits with code 1 — **F-001-RQ-004**, assumption **A-002** |

#### 8.1.1.2 Geographic Distribution Requirements

There are none. The addressable surface of the system is one machine's loopback interface, a boundary §1.3 records as the system boundary and which this section re-verified by probing the host's routable address (connection refused).

| Distribution concern | Requirement | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Multi-region or multi-zone placement | None | A loopback listener cannot be fronted by any regional endpoint (**C-002**) |
| CDN or edge caching | None | The single 14-byte response is generated in-process; no static asset or origin pull exists |
| DNS, service discovery, or global load balancing | None | No hostname other than the literal `127.0.0.1` appears anywhere in the tree |
| Data residency or locality constraint | None | The entire data domain is one compile-time string literal and two configuration constants; nothing is stored (§1.3) |
| Latency-driven placement | Not applicable | Client and server are always on the same host; measured host-local latency is p50 0.138 ms for new connections and p50 0.064 ms on reused connections (§6.5.3.2) |

#### 8.1.1.3 Network Architecture

The network architecture is a single listening socket on the loopback interface. There is no proxy, no TLS termination, no gateway, and no firewall configuration in the repository — and none is required, because the kernel itself refuses every non-loopback approach to port 3000.

| Network element | Configuration | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bind address and port | `127.0.0.1:3000`, hard-coded at `server.js` lines 3–4 and applied by `server.listen(port, hostname, …)` at line 12 | Repository code |
| Protocol | Cleartext HTTP/1.1; no TLS, no certificate material, no `https` module usage | Repository code (by omission) |
| Connection framing headers | `Content-Length`, `Date`, `Connection: keep-alive`, `Keep-Alive: timeout=5` | Node.js runtime defaults, not repository configuration — constraint **C-004** |
| Off-host reachability | None; the routable interface has no listener, so connections are refused (`curl` exit 7, code `000`) | Kernel, as a consequence of the loopback bind |
| Egress | None; §3.4 records zero outbound sockets and no HTTP-client, DNS, or socket-connect call in the tree | Repository code (by omission) |

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    LOCAL["Host-local client<br/>curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/"]
    REMOTE["Off-host client<br/>any other machine or namespace"]
    subgraph HostKernel["Host kernel network stack"]
        LO["Loopback interface lo<br/>127.0.0.1"]
        NIC["Routable interface<br/>host address, e.g. 10.76.1.16"]
        SOCK["Listening socket<br/>proc-net-tcp key 0100007F:0BB8 state 0A"]
        REFUSED["No listener bound<br/>kernel refuses - curl exit 7, code 000"]
        LO --> SOCK
        NIC --> REFUSED
    end
    APP["node process request handler<br/>200 / text/plain / 14 bytes<br/>identical for every method and path"]
    LOCAL --> LO
    REMOTE --> NIC
    SOCK --> APP
    subgraph AbsentNet["Network infrastructure verified absent"]
        TLSTERM["TLS termination and certificates"]
        PROXY["Reverse proxy or API gateway"]
        FWRULE["Firewall rules, security groups, NACLs"]
        DNSREC["DNS records and service discovery"]
    end
```

#### 8.1.1.4 Resource Requirements

All figures below were measured by executing a disposable copy of the repository on the verification host (Node.js v22.23.1, npm 11.18.0, 16 logical CPUs, ~127.8 GB RAM — an environment observation, since the repository pins no runtime, **D-005**). The repository itself declares no resource requirement, no limit, and no threshold of any kind.

| Resource dimension | Measured or observed requirement | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compute | One process, one JavaScript thread; 7 OS threads and ~0.18 s CPU for ~1,300 requests on a 16-CPU host | `server.js` contains no `cluster`, `worker_threads`, or `child_process` usage; thread and CPU figures cross-referenced from §6.5.3.5 |
| Memory | RSS ≈ 46.9 MB at idle (heapTotal ≈ 5.6 MB, heapUsed ≈ 4.7 MB, external ≈ 1.7 MB); VmRSS 48.2 MB at start rising to 61.9 MB after 25,000 requests, only +268 kB across the final 20,000 | `process.memoryUsage()` on Node v22.23.1 (this section); growth envelope from §6.5.3.5 |
| Storage — source | 913 bytes for the entire working tree across four files; 188 KB for the `.git` object store | `du` on the checkout; `git clone` reproduced a 913-byte working tree in 7 ms |
| Storage — dependencies | 0 bytes; `npm ci` exits 0 and creates no `node_modules` | `package-lock.json` locks only the root package (`lockfileVersion: 3`, one `""` entry); `npm ci` measured at 188/181/179 ms |
| Storage — runtime prerequisite | ~119 MiB for the Node.js binary itself (environment observation, not a repository declaration) | `/usr/bin/node` on the verification host |
| Storage — data and logs | 0 bytes, permanently; no filesystem write, no log file, no database | No `fs` usage in `server.js`; §6.5 records zero log or storage growth under sustained load |
| Network | One inbound TCP listener; 14-byte response body; no egress socket ever opened | `server.js` lines 6–10 and 12; egress census in §3.4 |
| File descriptors | Constant 22 while serving | §6.5.3.5 |

#### 8.1.1.5 Resource Sizing Guidelines

The system has no scaling dimension: throughput is bounded by one process on one host, and §2.4.3 records that horizontal scaling is structurally excluded because the loopback bind admits no external traffic and adding `cluster` support would require a source change forbidden by **C-001**/**F-006**. Sizing therefore reduces to *"any host that can run Node.js has ample headroom"*.

| Sizing dimension | Minimum to run | Guidance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| vCPU | 1 | Measured throughput was ~12,300–12,761 requests/second sequentially on the verification host (§6.5.3.2); a second vCPU adds nothing because JavaScript execution is single-threaded |
| RAM | ~64 MB free for the process, plus the OS baseline | Idle RSS ≈ 46.9 MB; the observed ceiling after 25,000 requests was 61.9 MB, so 128 MB is a comfortable allocation and 256 MB is generous |
| Disk | ~120 MB (dominated entirely by the Node.js runtime) | The repository contributes 913 bytes of source and 188 KB of git history; no build output, no dependencies, no data files |
| Network | One free TCP port (3000) on the loopback interface | Assumption **A-002**; automation must serialise its use of port 3000 because a second instance fails with `EADDRINUSE` |
| Scale-out unit | None | One instance per host is the maximum (§3.6.3); scaling by adding hosts does not aggregate capacity because no load balancer can reach a loopback listener |

#### 8.1.1.6 Compliance and Regulatory Requirements

No compliance or regulatory requirement is expressed or implicated by this repository — a determination §2.4.4 already records and which the deployment-environment evidence independently supports.

| Compliance dimension | Status | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Regulated data handling (PII, PHI, PCI, financial) | None | The complete data domain is one static 14-byte greeting plus two configuration literals; the request object is never dereferenced, so no client data is read, logged, or stored (**F-002-RQ-004**) |
| Data retention, residency, or right-to-erasure obligations | None | Nothing is persisted anywhere; §1.3 records no data domain requiring retention, encryption, or backup |
| Audit-trail obligation | None declared | The only telemetry is a single readiness line (`server.js` line 13); §6.5 records that stdout remains exactly one line after 25,000 requests, so no access log exists to retain |
| Encryption-in-transit mandate | None declared, none implemented | Cleartext HTTP on loopback only; traffic never leaves the host |
| Licensing and distribution terms | MIT, declared as a string only | `license: "MIT"` in `package.json` and mirrored in the `package-lock.json` root record; **no `LICENSE` file exists** in the tree |
| Change-control obligation | Self-imposed content freeze | `README.md` line 2 ("Do not touch!") is the governing control — **C-001**; the single-commit history is the audit record |

### 8.1.2 Environment Management

#### 8.1.2.1 Infrastructure as Code Approach

There is no Infrastructure-as-Code approach, because there is no infrastructure to codify. An exhaustive filename audit of the repository returned **zero** hits for every provisioning technology class probed.

| IaC technology class | Artefacts probed | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Terraform / OpenTofu | `*.tf`, `*.tfvars`, `*.hcl` | Absent |
| AWS CloudFormation / CDK | `*cloudformation*`, `*template*.json`, `cdk.json` | Absent |
| Pulumi / Azure Bicep / ARM | `Pulumi*`, `*.bicep` | Absent |
| Configuration management | `ansible*`, `playbook*`, Chef, Puppet layouts | Absent |
| Local machine provisioning | `Vagrantfile`, `Makefile*`, `*.sh`, `*.bat`, `*.ps1` | Absent |

Two independent semantic index queries — one for deployment/Dockerfile/CI/IaC definitions and one for folders holding build automation, release pipelines, orchestration manifests, or provisioning scripts — both returned empty result sets, corroborating the filename audit. As a further environment-level observation, the verification host on which the repository was exercised has **no `terraform`, `kubectl`, `helm`, `docker`, or `make` binary installed at all**, so no provisioning workflow could have been executed even implicitly.

The functional substitute for IaC in this system is `git clone` plus `node server.js`: the environment is fully described by the Node.js runtime being present and TCP port 3000 being free.

#### 8.1.2.2 Configuration Management Strategy

The configuration management strategy is **compile-time literals with no override path**, recorded as constraint **C-003**.

| Configuration concern | How it is handled here | Consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bind address and port | Source literals `const hostname = '127.0.0.1'` and `const port = 3000` (`server.js` lines 3–4) | Changing either requires editing tracked content, which **C-001** forbids |
| Environment variables | None consumed anywhere; content grep across all four files finds no `process.env` | No 12-factor style configuration, no per-environment values, no feature flags |
| Command-line arguments | None consumed; no `process.argv` reference exists | The process cannot be parameterised at launch |
| Configuration files | None; no `.env`, `.env.example`, `.npmrc`, `.nvmrc`, `.node-version`, `tsconfig*`, or `*.config.js` exists | Nothing to template, seed, or inject per environment |
| Secrets management | Not applicable — no credential, token, key, or certificate exists in the tree (§2.4.4) | No vault, parameter store, or sealed-secret integration is needed |
| Runtime version pinning | Absent — `package.json` declares no `engines` field | Deviation **D-005**: the runtime is whatever the host provides, and Node.js default behaviour (e.g. the framing headers of **C-004**) is therefore part of the observable contract without being under repository control |

#### 8.1.2.3 Environment Promotion Strategy

There is no dev/staging/prod topology to promote between. The repository defines exactly one environment — the host on which the process is started — and the git history shows no release engineering activity of any kind.

| Commit history | Exactly one commit, `1a0874d`, with the message "Add files via upload" | Indicates a bulk web-UI upload rather than an engineered release flow; §2.5 treats this commit as the requirement baseline |
| Environment-specific configuration | None (see 8.1.2.2) | Even if multiple environments existed, the identical hard-coded `127.0.0.1:3000` would be used in each |

#### 8.1.2.4 Backup and Disaster Recovery

The system holds no state, so disaster recovery is reduced to restoring four immutable text files.

| DR concern | Position | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What must be protected | Only the four tracked files (913 bytes total) | The process writes nothing to disk; §6.5 records zero storage growth under load |
| Durable copies | The GitHub `origin` repository, the local 188 KB `.git` object store, and the working tree | `git remote -v` shows a single HTTPS `origin` for the GitHub repository `Sandeep01Kumar/28-july-existing-projects-qa-test-01` (the URL carries an ephemeral checkout credential supplied by the environment, not stored in any tracked file) |
| Recovery procedure | `git clone` the repository, then `node server.js` | Measured: 7 ms local clone; §6.5 records a ~23 ms process restart and 26.9–34 ms to readiness |
| Recovery point objective | Effectively zero data loss | There is no mutable data; content is versioned and frozen at commit `1a0874d` (**F-006-RQ-003**) |
| Backup schedule, snapshots, replication | None exist and none is required | No database, volume, object store, or cache is present (§3.5, §8.2) |
| Failure mode with operator impact | Port 3000 already bound | Unhandled `EADDRINUSE`, exit code 1, no retry and no fallback port; the operator must free the port or stop the other instance (§6.5 runbooks RB-01…RB-04) |
| Process supervision / auto-restart | None | No systemd unit, PM2 ecosystem file, or supervisor config exists; `server.js` registers no `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT` handler, so termination is immediate and silent |

#### 8.1.2.5 Minimal Build and Distribution Requirements

Per the section prompt's guidance for systems that need no deployment infrastructure, the following is the complete build-and-distribution requirement set. §3.6.2 states the position precisely: there is no build system, and **the tracked tree *is* the artefact**.

| Requirement | Specification | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Runtime | A Node.js runtime supporting CommonJS `require` and the core `http` module (assumption **A-001**); no version constraint is declared (**D-005**) | Verified on Node.js v22.23.1 |
| Build step | None — no transpilation, bundling, minification, or native compilation | No `tsconfig*`, bundler config, or build script exists; the only npm script is `test` |
| Dependency installation | Optional and inert: `npm ci` exits 0, audits one package, reports zero vulnerabilities, and creates no `node_modules` | Measured 188/181/179 ms; `npm ci --offline` also exits 0, so **no registry or internet access is required** |
| Tooling assumption | If manifest tooling is used, it must understand `lockfileVersion: 3` (assumption **A-005**) | `package-lock.json` declares `"lockfileVersion": 3` with a single root entry |
| Distribution channel | Git only; the repository is not publishable as a package | `package.json` declares no `files`, `publishConfig`, `repository`, `bin`, or `private` field (§3.6.2); `main: "index.js"` points at a file that does not exist, so `require('hello_world')` fails with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` — deviation **D-001**, constraint **C-005** |
| Launch | `node server.js`; `npm start` works only through npm's implicit default because a `server.js` exists at the package root — deviation **D-004** | Both verified; the readiness line `Server running at http://127.0.0.1:3000/` is emitted from `server.js` line 13 (**F-003-RQ-001**) |
| Host prerequisites | Read-only access to the four files, one free loopback TCP port, no credentials | §3.6.7 |
